Voat, what is your favorite childhood memory?

I remember when I was a kid I would always play cops 'n' robbers with my friends in our neighborhood. I was REALLY good at hiding, and I was fast too so I never went to jail. My friends all told me I was the best hider and whenever it was just me they would just switch sides and not tell me because I was hiding too well. So I would always end up running away from the robbers when I was the cop because no one told me. Childhood was fun.

In one of my schools, which only had a concrete playground, we'd play a COPS version of Cops and Robbers. After the robber was tackled, they'd be dragged over to the fence and their arms would be wrapped around these metal chains with hooks attached to them. I don't know why the schoolyard had these... though it's kinda weird that the priests house overlooked that exact spot where the chains were.
I would dig holes with my hands in the mud on a river near my backyard. No real purpose in mind just to see how far I could get without it collapsing. I would love to do that again these days.
Yeah! I remember trying to see if I could get two holes to connect at the beach to make a little tunnel.
Watching multiple episodes of Simpsons in a row, because different stations would play them at different times.

Summers playing with the neighbours. Tip the can, football, fishing and rolling down hills in a barrel is what the entire day would consist of! We lived rurally so we were surrounded by loads of fields we could play in. I rarely talk to those people now, strange how people drift apart.
Building my fist computer. It was only okay even then. But I loved that thing.
Saturday morning cartoons, definitely. I loved waking up early in the morning and binge watching what where probably mostly terrible shows. Nothing can compare to the pure joy i felt those mornings.

The lack of communication between the Admins and Moderators/Users caused all of the tensions that had been building to boil over. The firing of Victoria was the straw that broke the camel's back.

The mods rallied and whilst both trying to raise awareness of how key a role Victoria filled and their anger over the suggestion that AMAs will become a source of revenue, closed their doors to all as a form of protest.

That, and Melton adds the ability to rest McCoy a bit more during games without an insane drop-off in talent -- keeping him in better condition hopefully throughout the year.

Honorable mention would be maybe the tight end position on offense. I really like ASJ, and with a full offseason to practice and train with the team, I expect he'll be better. Getting Tim Wright back was really great and can add another dimension to the offense with two receiving tight ends on the field in two TE sets. Stocker, as much as he has struggled as a receiver, has been a really good blocker. Myers can do a bit of both and provides a nice bit of depth.
